claude.sample_unit: model responses (80 vignettes x 3 prompt types)

links.outcome: Safety-critical under-triage of red-flag shoulder/elbow vignettes by LLM
links.effect: Under-triage in 19 of 72 red-flag responses (26.4%); urgency correctly recognized in 53 (73.6%); patient-oriented prompts 10/24 (41.7%).
links.quote: Across the 72 prompt-specific responses derived from the 24 red-flag vignettes (24 vignettes × 3 prompt conditions), correct urgency classification was observed in 53 responses (73.6%), whereas safety-critical under-triage occurred in 19 responses (26.4%).

links.outcome: LLM recognition of safety-critical situations and urgent escalation; missed and unnecessary escalations
links.effect: Under-triage 26.4% of red-flag responses (41.7% patient prompts); over-triage in 3 of 56 non-urgent vignettes (5.4%).
links.quote: Inappropriate emergency department referral (over-triage), defined as emergency department referral in the absence of supporting red-flag features, occurred in 3 of 56 non-urgent vignettes (5.4%).

links.outcome: Decision stability under single-variable input changes (paired vignettes)
links.effect: Decision instability in 6 of 20 paired vignette sets (30.0%), mostly failure to raise urgency after a red-flag modifier was added.
links.quote: Decision instability was observed in 6 of the 20 vignette pairs (30.0%).

links.outcome: False reassurance/delay-inducing reassurance in single-turn red-flag responses
links.effect: Errors mostly under-recognition of urgency and delay-inducing reassurance; multi-turn simulation not assessed; single-turn under-triage 26.4%.
links.quote: These events were more commonly related to under-recognition of urgency and delay-inducing reassurance than to clinically inappropriate therapeutic recommendations.
